title: Narrow governance repair: CLOSED-Task cross-baseline revalidation and PG-001 HOLD dependency path

why5.question: Why can BS-P1-025 not be activated on main dbfdc948 without changing any CLOSED Task?
why5.answer: BD-025 changes the criterion/expected_observable of 10 ACTIVE Acceptances (test_id unchanged). Rebinding SP-P1-003 to BS-P1-025 makes CLOSED T001 (BS-P1-021; F01-AC-013/016) fail 'baseline mismatch', DONE BL-P1-010 fail 'backlog baseline mismatch', and BL-P1-008 (already revalidated to BS-P1-024 by CLOSED T007) need a new revalidation whose only slot holds the CLOSED T007 record.

why5.question: Why is editing the CLOSED Task or overwriting the CLOSED revalidation not acceptable?
why5.answer: CLOSED Tasks and CLOSED revalidations are completion history. The only lawful options in dbfdc948 are rebinding T001 to BS-P1-025 (rewrites a CLOSED Task) or replacing BL-P1-008.revalidation (destroys the T007 record); both falsify history. No validator guarded either against a later diff.
why5.evidence_ref: harness/scripts/validate-change-scope.mjs at dbfdc948: immutableTasks() only applies to safeControlTransition, not to rebaseline transitions; validate-backlog.mjs resolveItemRevalidationIds() requires revalidation.target_build_spec_id = current baseline

why5.question: What exact validator change resolves the cross-baseline case while keeping CLOSED records byte-identical?
why5.answer: (1) DONE items may carry an append-only revalidation_history of CLOSED revalidations; each entry must cover exactly the drift of its own step and the new revalidation covers only chain-end -> current drift. (2) A CLOSED Task at an ancestor baseline whose claims drifted stays unchanged; its drifted claims are superseded only when a revalidation listed by the Sprint assigns them to a different Task. (3) A selected DONE item may be revalidated inside its own Sprint. (4) Change-scope now rejects any diff that edits, reopens or deletes a CLOSED Task, or that overwrites/drops a CLOSED revalidation instead of appending it to revalidation_history.

why5.question: Why does PG-001 need a dedicated HOLD path for package.json and package-lock.json?
why5.answer: package.json is governance_only (forbidden during any active Task and in allowed_write_paths), while package-lock.json is an implementation root that change-scope rejects whenever Sprint is HOLD. So pg@8.23.0 / @types/pg@8.23.1 had no lawful landing state. The new path accepts only: Sprint HOLD, implementation disabled, no control-state change, exactly package.json + package-lock.json + one docket, package.json identical except the two exact additions, every existing lock entry byte-identical, and only allow-listed npm-registry tarballs with sha512 integrity added.
